questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security guardrails for S3 exposure, emphasizing concrete steps over theory.

## Key Concepts
- S3 public-access controls and explicit policy posture
- Data protection: encryption and versioning
- IAM Access Analyzer and SNS alerting
- Lightweight testing and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```bash
# Block public access account-wide
aws s3control put-public-access-block --account-id <acct> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true

# Enable encryption and versioning
aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket <BUCKET> --server-side-encryption-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault":{"SSEAlgorithm":"AES256"}}]}'
aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket <BUCKET> --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled

# Wire analyzer findings to SNS (example)
aws accessanalyzer create-analyzer --type ACCOUNT --name Guardrails --tags Purpose=Security
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this guardrail with a controlled misconfiguration?
- How would you handle exceptions for legitimate public assets?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical cross-region disaster recovery knowledge with real AWS services and automation capabilities. Evaluates understanding of RTO/RPO constraints, service integration, and operational readiness.

## Key Concepts
- Cross-region RDS read replicas with automated promotion
- S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) with Replication Time Control
- Route 53 health checks and failover routing policies
- Cross-account IAM trust relationships and role-based access
- CloudWatch alarm-driven automation via EventBridge/Step Functions

## Code Example
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: DR Stack - Cross-Region Failover Resources
Resources:
  DRRDSReadReplica:
    Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
    Properties:
      SourceDBInstanceIdentifier: !Sub 'arn:aws:rds:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:db:prod-primary'
      DBInstanceClass: db.t3.medium
      AvailabilityZone: us-west-2a
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: dr

  DRDataLakeBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Sub 'datalake-dr-${AWS::AccountId}'
      ReplicationConfiguration:
        Role: !GetAtt ReplicationRole.Arn
        Rules:
          - Destination:
              Bucket: !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:::datalake-dr'
              StorageClass: STANDARD
            ID: CRR-Rule
            Status: Enabled
            SourceSelectionCriteria:
              Ssecs:
                SseAwsKmsKeyId: !Ref DataLakeKey

  ReplicationRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: s3.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole

  Route53FailoverRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      SetIdentifier: primary
      Failover:
        Type: PRIMARY
      HealthCheckId: !Ref PrimaryHealthCheck
      AliasTarget:
        DNSName: !GetAtt PrimaryALB.DNSName
        HostedZoneId: !GetAtt PrimaryALB.CanonicalHostedZoneID

  Route53DRRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      Name: api.example.com
      Type: A
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      SetIdentifier: dr
      Failover:
        Type: SECONDARY
      AliasTarget:
        DNSName: !GetAtt DRALB.DNSName
        HostedZoneId: !GetAtt DRALB.CanonicalHostedZoneID

  PrimaryHealthCheck:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HealthCheck
    Properties:
      HealthCheckConfig:
        Type: HTTPS
        FullyQualifiedDomainName: api.example.com
        Port: 443
        ResourcePath: /health
        RequestInterval: 30
        FailureThreshold: 3
```
